title: [FMLA 01] QuadEquation — Quadratic Equation Solution
summary: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 for real roots. Two distinct roots, one repeated root, or MATH ERROR when there are no real roots.

body.text: Calculator scroll name: QuadEquation. Solves the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 for real roots. Enter coefficients a, b, and c when prompted (a ≠ 0).
The calculator uses the discriminant D = b² − 4ac internally. How many real roots you get depends on D:

items: D > 0 — two distinct real roots (shown one after another; press EXE to see the second)
D = 0 — one real root (a repeated / double root); both displays are the same value
D < 0 — no real roots; the calculator shows MATH ERROR

body.text: MATH ERROR on FMLA 01 means there are no real roots (complex conjugate roots exist, but this built-in formula does not display them). For complex-style output, use a custom PRGM such as the sample quadratic solver under Programming.

body.title: Open QuadEquation
items: Press FMLA, then 0, then 1 (or scroll to QuadEquation and EXE)
Enter a, then b, then c at each prompt
Read the first root; press EXE again for the second root when two are shown
two real roots: x = 4 and x = 3

body.caption: Same example: y = x² − 7x + 12. The curve hits the axis at the two roots the calculator prints, x = 3 and x = 4.

body.title: Key strokes
items: Display: 3 (and again 3 on the next EXE)
no real roots — FMLA 01 shows MATH ERROR

body.title: Key strokes
items: Display: MATH ERROR — means no real roots for this equation

body.text: Always confirm a ≠ 0. If a = 0 the equation is not quadratic and the routine is not valid. For complex roots or vertex output in one program, see [[modes/prgm/example/quadratic]].
